beginner.summary: For cloud, DevOps and application engineers who can write simple TypeScript or Python and are new to Pulumi. Covers installing the Pulumi CLI, projects and Pulumi.yaml, stacks, the preview, update, refresh and destroy workflow, resources, URNs and auto-naming, inputs and outputs, stack configuration and encrypted secrets, stack outputs, resource options, provider functions, explicit providers, the Pulumi Cloud backend, reading diffs, ordinary language constructs in programs, a comparison with Go, C# and YAML, debugging failed updates, and a website-plus-API capstone on AWS.
prerequisites: Writes small programs in TypeScript or Python: functions, lists, dictionaries or objects, and installing packages with npm or pip
Understands basic cloud concepts such as regions, IAM users and roles, object storage and serverless functions
Has a laptop with Node.js LTS and Python 3.10 or later, an AWS sandbox account with credentials configured for the AWS CLI, and an editor such as Visual Studio Code
outcomes: Create Pulumi projects and stacks in TypeScript and Python and run preview, up, refresh and destroy confidently
Model cloud resources with inputs, outputs, resource options and explicit providers, and read the resulting diffs
Manage per-stack configuration and encrypted secrets without leaking values into source control or logs
Deliver a small multi-resource AWS stack with exported outputs and diagnose failed updates from CLI output

intermediate.summary: For engineers who already run Pulumi stacks in TypeScript or Python and now need to share, secure and govern them across a team. Covers component resources and packaging, stack references, self-managed S3 state with KMS secrets providers, state export, import and repair, Pulumi ESC environments with OIDC credentials, the Kubernetes provider with manifests, Helm and an EKS cluster, unit tests with mocks, property tests through policy packs, CrossGuard policies, CI pipelines, importing existing resources, converting Terraform HCL, refactoring with aliases, transforms, drift detection with refresh, and a multi-stack platform capstone.
prerequisites: Completed the beginner level or has deployed and maintained several Pulumi stacks with config, secrets and outputs
Comfortable with TypeScript classes and async code or Python classes, plus npm or pip packaging
Has access to an AWS sandbox account with rights to create EKS, IAM, KMS and S3 resources, kubectl and Helm installed, and a GitHub repository for CI exercises
outcomes: Build, test and publish reusable component resources and connect stacks through stack references
Operate Pulumi state on Pulumi Cloud or S3, repair it safely and manage credentials with Pulumi ESC
Deploy Kubernetes workloads and an EKS cluster with the Pulumi Kubernetes provider
Enforce standards with unit tests, CrossGuard policy packs and CI previews, and bring existing or Terraform-managed infrastructure under Pulumi

advanced.summary: For platform engineers and infrastructure leads who own Pulumi across many teams, accounts and clusters. Covers the Automation API in TypeScript and Python, orchestrating multi-stack rollouts, integration testing with ephemeral stacks, Pulumi Deployments with review and TTL stacks, scheduled drift detection and remediation, dynamic providers, multi-language component packages, bridging Terraform providers, large Terraform-to-Pulumi migrations, organization-wide policy enforcement, ESC at scale, the Pulumi Kubernetes Operator, multi-cluster and multi-account providers, performance of large stacks, recovery from interrupted updates, Pulumi Cloud access control and audit, advanced resource lifecycle options, provider supply-chain control, resource insights, and a self-service platform capstone.
prerequisites: Completed the intermediate level or has run Pulumi in production with components, stack references, CI pipelines and policy packs
Builds services in TypeScript or Python, reads Go, and understands REST APIs, containers and Kubernetes controllers
Has a Pulumi Cloud organization with admin rights or a trial that includes Deployments and policies, plus sandbox AWS accounts and a Kubernetes cluster
outcomes: Embed Pulumi in services and orchestrate rollouts across many stacks with the Automation API and Pulumi Deployments
Extend Pulumi with dynamic providers, multi-language components and bridged Terraform providers
Migrate large Terraform estates and recover state safely from failures and drift
Govern Pulumi at organization scale with policies, ESC, access control, audit logs and resource insights
